key_insight: High-resolution power traces from generative-AI workloads can be systematically mapped to whole-facility energy and capacity models, revealing transient peaks and duty-cycle behavior that materially change infrastructure sizing and energy estimates.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between proprietary, component-level power measurements and whole-facility data center planning by providing a methodology to translate workload-level power into facility-scale energy, peak demand, and infrastructure requirements.
method: Collect high-resolution workload power measurements (server/GPU, rack, PDU) while running representative generative-AI tasks to capture transients and steady-state behaviors.
Map component-level traces into facility systems (cooling, UPS, PDUs) using empirical/system models and adjust with PUE and transient multipliers to produce whole-facility power profiles.

Aggregate and simulate planning scenarios (peak provisioning, energy totals, diversity factors, temporal scheduling) to derive capacity, cooling, and resiliency requirements for infrastructure planning.
impact: Provides AI/ML engineers and data center planners actionable, empirically grounded inputs to size power delivery and cooling correctly, reduce overprovisioning, and optimize scheduling, cost, and carbon accounting for generative-AI workloads.
visual_elements: Time-series line chart of high-resolution workload power showing transient spikes vs average
Stacked bar or waterfall chart mapping compute power to facility-level components (compute → PDU/UPS → cooling → total)
Sankey or flow diagram from server/GPU measurements through aggregation, PUE adjustment, and whole-facility output
Scenario matrix heatmap of peak demand vs job scheduling strategies (shows sensitivity and planning outcomes)
paper_title: Measurement of Generative AI Workload Power Profiles for Whole-Facility Data Center Infrastructure Planning
paper_authors: Roberto Vercellino, Jared Willard, Gustavo Campos, Weslley da Silva Pereira, Olivia Hull
